newsitem.title: USA: Ball to close metal food can plant.
newsitem.headline: Ball to close metal food can plant.

text.p: Ball Corp said on Monday that it will close its metal food can plant in Columbus, Ind and redeploy or dispose of certain beverage container manufacturing assets at its Baie d'Urfe, Quebec, Canada plant.

In the fourth quarter, the company will record costs associated with the Columbus closing, Baie d'Urfe disposition of assets and certain other actions designed to streamline the company's metal container operations.
Ball previously said it would record a gain in the fourth quarter resulting from the sale of its interest in Ball-Foster Glass Container Co LLC.
It said the Columbus plant, which employs about 180 people, is expected to close on December 2. Employees there will be paid through mid-January.

In Baie d'Urfe, production from the plant's two aluminum beverage can lines will cease. Ball anticipates shifting production equipment from the beverage can lines to certain international affiliates. The Baie d'Urfe plant will continue to operate as a food can manufacturing plant.

"These and other actions will result in a higher rate of capacity utilization and a more competitive cost structure in our manufacturing operations," George Sissel, Ball's chairman, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

"We are positioning ourselves to compete more effectively in mature North American markets, as well as expanding in growth markets here and internationally," Sissel said. "While short-term performance, including 1996 fourth-quarter and full-year results, will not be as strong as we would have hoped, we will be a considerably different company in 1997 as a result of our actions."
Ball produces rigid packaging materials, primarily for foods and beverages and provides aerospace and other technologies and services to the government and commercial markets.
